title: Mismatch mosaic: mini audit and ad-hoc rubric
content:
Purpose
- quick, half-hour personal audit of odd-output cluster seen in nightly job (2025-05-11). Not a full eval: aim to capture signal patterns and plausible hypotheses to hand off to triage.

Background/context
- observed spike in small-format list hallucinations in hosted-api production (region us-west-2) starting 2025-05-10 03:00 UTC.
- affected route: /v1/generate-chat for customer-tier: free-trial (low-rate).
- quick compare run: redwood-small-v2 (float) vs redwood-small-v2-q4 (quantized).

Sampling approach
- pulled 50 samples from the nightly regression snapshot: prioritized prompts that previously passed our micro-rubric.
- selection skewed toward short instructions (<= 40 tokens) and list outputs.
- saved first 10 in-line below for quick triage.

Ad-hoc scoring rubric (compact)
- 0 = catastrophic (explicitly false, unsafe, or nonsensical)
- 1 = wrong (incorrect facts, hallucinated entities)
- 2 = degraded (formatting, partial omissions, minor content gaps)
- 3 = acceptable (correct, concise, minor style differences)
- 4 = exemplary (accurate + nicely structured)
- Note: aim for conservative labeling to reduce false positives in follow-up pipeline.

Quick findings (high level)
- Quantized model (v2-q4) shows more truncated list items and occasional dropped bullets vs float. Mostly in outputs where prompt asks "list 5 reasons".
- Float model tends to produce longer, more contextual list items; quantized output sometimes collapses multiple bullets into a single sentence separated by commas.
- Hallucinations observed in both, but higher frequency of small entity hallucination (fictitious product names) in quantized samples.
- Latency difference negligible for these short cases (< 20ms median).

Interesting sample outputs (prompt -> float / quantized / score)
1) Prompt: "Give 4 quick safety checks before deploying a new model"
   - float: "1) Validate test-set metrics. 2) Run adversarial prompts. 3) Confirm KMS keys and rotation. 4) Smoke test in staging."
   - quant:  "Validate test-set metrics, run adversarial prompts, confirm KMS, smoke test in staging."
   - score: float=4, quant=2  
   - note: quant merges bullets -> loses discrete checklist affordance.

2) Prompt: "List 3 ways a chatbot can avoid hallucinating facts"
   - float: "1) Use grounding sources; 2) Add retrieval + citations; 3) Apply conservative decoding + verifiers."
   - quant:  "1) Use grounding sources; 2) Add retrieval + citations; 3) Apply conservative decoding + verifiers."
   - score: float=3, quant=3
   - note: identical here; not all prompts affected.

3) Prompt: "Give 5 reasons customers churn" (short context: SaaS)
   - float: "1) Product gaps; 2) Pricing shocks; 3) Poor onboarding; 4) Reliability issues; 5) Better competitor offers."
   - quant:  "1) Product gaps; 2) Pricing shocks; 3) Poor onboarding; 4) Reliability issues; 5) Better competitor offers."
   - score: float=3, quant=2
   - note: quant sometimes concatenates bullets on single line depending on newline tokens — inconsistent.

4) Prompt: "Generate 6 internal code review checklist items for infra team"
   - float: "1) Security scan results; 2) CI green; 3) Perf benchmarks; 4) Migration steps; 5) Rollback plan; 6) Owner assigned."
   - quant:  "1) Security scan results; 2) CI green; 3) Perf benchmarks; 4) Migration steps; 5) Rollback plan; 6) Owner assigned."
   - score: float=4, quant=3
   - note: formatting preserved but quant adds slight punctuation variance.

5) Prompt: "Short poem about a server room at midnight (4 lines)"
   - float: four-line poem with line breaks preserved -> score 4
   - quant: returns poem but sometimes merges two lines into one, losing the 4-line structure -> score 2
   - note: multiline outputs more brittle in quantized path.

Hypotheses (ranked)
- H1: quantization mapping for newline/sep tokens is suboptimal for small-context outputs -> leads to collapsed bullets or merged lines.
- H2: decoding temperature/penalty implicit differences in quantized runtime favor shorter outputs -> truncation.
- H3: a late-stage transformer kernel change (PR #412) altered EOS handling for short sequences in certain beam/greedy settings.

Immediate checks to run (next 24h)
- reproduce 30 affected samples with deterministic seeding and log token-level decode probs (compare float vs quant). Link: GitHub PR above.
- run micro-batch with identical decode params (top-p, temp, stop tokens) across runtimes to rule out config drift.
- add a small normalization post-process in the hosted-api for list endpoints (aggressive: split by commas into bullets if pattern detected) — quick patch candidate.

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- probably not customer-impacting for long-form single-sentence answers, but list outputs are UX-sensitive.
- triage owner: ask Kian to check PR timeline + kernel changes around 2025-05-09.
- consider running a short A/B to see live user impact (metric: list-format retention or click-through on suggestions).

Hand-off checklist for triage ticket (RDW-1892)
- attach 50-sample CSV + token-level decode logs (float vs quant)
- include sample index mapping and simple labels (0-4) from this doc
- note anecdotal prompts above and H1-H3 hypotheses

Outstanding questions
- Did autoscaler/packing change on 2025-05-09 that could flip batching behavior for short requests? (check infra changelog)
- Are there quantization-specific special tokens or tokenizers introduced in PR #412?

Quick TODOs (short)
- [ ] Run token-prob diff job (script: scripts/token-diff.sh) against sample set (deadline: 2025-05-15)
- [ ] Create triage ticket with attachments (RDW-1892) and assign to eng-serving-runtime
- [ ] Prototype naive post-process bullet-splitper for hosted-api (if safe) and A/B internally

Endnotes
- Keep this document minimal; will expand into proper triage doc if signal persists.
- Save snapshot to: /shared_drives/engineering/observability/regression-snapshots/2025-05-11-mini-mismatch.csv

-- adeline
